story_type: Mach 3 spy jet flies a rocket engine experiment on its back, air to air
hook: The fastest jet ever flown in service, with a rocket on its back.
narration: The fastest production jet ever built, flying with a rocket experiment on its back.
The SR-71 could fly more than twenty two hundred miles per hour, above eighty five thousand feet.
The Air Force loaned these Blackbirds to NASA for high speed research at Edwards, California.
This one carried a test of the Linear Aerospike Rocket Engine, planned for the X-33 spaceplane.
An aerospike shapes its exhaust along a ramp instead of a bell nozzle, so it stays efficient from the ground to space.
outcome: This jet, NASA 844, flew the last SR-71 flight ever, in 1999.
title: SR-71 with a rocket engine on its back
description:
NASA's SR-71 Blackbird flies over California's Mojave Desert in 1998 carrying the Linear Aerospike Rocket Engine experiment, a propulsion concept planned for the X-33 technology demonstrator.
